name: abnormal and post-menopausal bleeding overview
title: Abnormal uterine bleeding divided by age: reproductive age split into structural (PALM) and functional (COEIN) causes, adolescence and perimenopause, and post-menopausal bleeding worked up in three numbered steps to a biopsy report that picks atrophy, hyperplasia or carcinoma; each column gives causes, history and exam, investigations and treatment

nodes.title: Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB): divide by AGE first
lines: any change in frequency, duration or amount of flow, or bleeding between cycles (dysfunctional uterine bleeding, DUB)
pre-pubertal: pediatrics · bleeding in pregnancy: see the FIRST-TRIMESTER BLEEDING chart

nodes.title: REPRODUCTIVE AGE: PALM-COEIN
lines: or the ABCs: Anatomic · Baby · Coagulopathy · DUB · Endocrine · Hormones · Infectious · Neoplasia
treat the cause; otherwise regulate the bleeding: medicines first, then move up

nodes.title: ADOLESCENCE + PERIMENOPAUSE
lines: both: higher rates of anovulation

nodes.title: POST-MENOPAUSAL: any bleeding after 12 months without menses
lines: ENDOMETRIAL CARCINOMA MUST BE EXCLUDED · commonest cause: atrophy

nodes.title: Work up every one, in order
lines: 1 · Vitals (is she STABLE?), history, general + abdominal + pelvic exam · SPECULUM, always: mass through the os, ulcerated cervix · a negative Pap test does not end it

2 · Transvaginal ultrasound: endometrium < 5 mm is normal (on HRT too: > 5 mm in over half, < 4% of those have pathology → investigate if bleeding persists) · > 5 mm → saline infusion sonohysterogram: finds focal lesions (93–100%) but CANNOT tell benign from malignant

3 · Sample: ENDOMETRIAL BIOPSY for > 5 mm, any post-menopausal bleeding, or recurrent bleeding at < 5 mm (4% of cancers are in that group) · 99.6% sensitive, but blind: misses polyps · HYSTEROSCOPY for focal lesions or a failed office biopsy · D&C only if both are unavailable or contraindicated (samples < 60% of the endometrium in half)

nodes.title: Structural: PALM
lines: Polyps · Adenomyosis · Leiomyoma (fibroids) · Malignancy + hyperplasia

nodes.title: Functional: COEIN
lines: Coagulopathy · Ovulatory dysfunction · Endometrial dysfunction · Iatrogenic · Not yet classified

nodes.title: Adolescence
lines: higher rates of anovulation

nodes.title: Perimenopause
lines: higher rates of anovulation
a huge reason for referrals + emergency visits

nodes.title: Atrophy (GSM)
lines: the most common cause

nodes.title: Endometrial hyperplasia
lines: overgrowth of the epithelium: gland:stroma ratio ↑, crowded glands
a PRECURSOR of carcinoma

nodes.title: Endometrial carcinoma
lines: #1 gynecologic malignancy · often curable, but can kill
endometrioid = the commonest type

nodes.title: ABCs: Anatomic
lines: fibroids, polyps, adenomyosis

nodes.title: ABCs: Neoplasia
lines: hyperplasia, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia

nodes.title: ABCs: Baby
lines: ectopic, abortion, implantation
~see the FIRST-TRIMESTER BLEEDING chart

nodes.title: ANOVULATION: the major underlying cause
lines: = DUB · walk down the axis; at each level ask: is the feedback working? did it form, and is its function compromised?

nodes.title: Hypothalamus
lines: gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) must be PULSATILE: stress, body mass (exercise, anorexia, malnutrition), chronic disease

nodes.title: Pituitary
lines: also makes thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) + prolactin (PRL): an abnormality in either interferes

nodes.title: Ovary
lines: follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) + luteinizing hormone (LH) → estrogen + progesterone · did it form, or get hurt?

nodes.title: Uterus + outflow tract
lines: did they form? is their function compromised or interrupted?

nodes.title: ABCs: C, E, H, I
lines: Coagulopathy: von Willebrand disease, thrombocytopenia, liver, leukemia
Endocrine: polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), TSH, PRL, Cushing
Hormones (exogenous): oral contraceptive pill (OCP), Depo, Mirena
Infectious: cervicitis, chlamydia, endometritis (sexually transmitted infections lecture)

nodes.title: Causes
lines: anovulation: immature hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis, 2 years to regular cycles
COAGULOPATHY: menarche can unmask it, most often von Willebrand

nodes.title: Causes
lines: usually anovulation, but MALIGNANCY rates are higher

nodes.title: HYPOESTROGENISM
lines: → microerosion, inflammation, spotting
bleeds from exposed small vessels: endometrium, vagina or vulva

nodes.title: Unopposed ESTROGEN
lines: ~the same risk factors as type 1 carcinoma

nodes.title: Endogenous
lines: obesity · PCOS · estrogen-secreting tumour (granulosa cell)
associations: infertility, nulliparity, early menarche, late menopause

nodes.title: Exogenous
lines: unopposed estrogen: HRT, topical
tamoxifen

nodes.title: HRT without a progestin
lines: NO unopposed systemic estrogen with a uterus: hyperplasia in 10% at 12 months, up to 50% at 24
cyclic estrogen + progestin: some risk with prolonged use

nodes.title: Type 1 · 90% · endometrioid
lines: ESTROGEN DEPENDENT: unopposed estrogen, same risk factors as hyperplasia
precursor: hyperplasia · better prognosis

nodes.title: Type 2 · 10% · usually serous
lines: estrogen INDEPENDENT: no unopposed estrogen
older patients, ATROPHIC endometrium · poorer prognosis

nodes.title: Lynch syndrome
lines: mismatch repair gene defects · 40–70% lifetime risk of endometrioid cancer, often the SENTINEL cancer

nodes.title: Inspection: vulva, vagina, cervix
lines: skin + colour change (atrophy, fissures) · abnormal discharge · lesions, irregular vascularity

nodes.title: Bimanual exam (palpation)
lines: UTERINE ENLARGEMENT: fibroids, adenomyosis, pregnancy
FIXATION · cancer

nodes.title: General appearance
lines: body habitus, BMI · BRUISING, PETECHIAE · cushingoid appearance
signs of thyroid disease · GALACTORRHEA · hirsutism, acne

nodes.title: Ask about
lines: eating disorder or ++ exercise
pregnancy

nodes.title: Can be severe, incapacitating, extreme
lines: the case: ventricular fibrillation arrest, hemoglobin 38
cycles had gone from 28 days with a pad every 4 h to every 14–45 days, 2–14 days of flow, a pad more than hourly, flooding, clots
~found because a clinician asked about her cycles

nodes.title: Vulvovaginal atrophy
lines: loss of labial fullness · pallor of urethral + vaginal epithelium
narrow introitus · minimal moisture · loss of urethral meatal turgor

nodes.title: Presents as
lines: post-menopausal bleeding
HRT: bleeding in 63% over the first 6 cycles

nodes.title: Presents as
lines: 90% vaginal bleeding · 72% at Stage 1 (confined to the uterine body)
cramping, pressure · pelvic exam normal or an enlarged uterus

nodes.title: Ultrasound
lines: imaging

nodes.title: Pap test ± swabs
lines: gonorrhea + chlamydia

nodes.title: Bloods
lines: complete blood count · international normalized ratio, partial thromboplastin time

nodes.title: Hormones
lines: FSH, LH, estradiol · TSH, PRL · 17-hydroxyprogesterone, androgen profile

nodes.title: Investigations
lines: remember the beta-hCG

nodes.title: Investigations
lines: remember to BIOPSY

nodes.title: Biopsy report #2
lines: scant fragments of atrophic endometrium

nodes.title: A diagnosis of EXCLUSION
lines: it must fit the other investigations

nodes.title: Report: without atypia
lines: malignancy risk: simple 1%, complex 3%

nodes.title: Report #3: ATYPICAL
lines: malignancy risk: simple 8%, complex 29%
30–40% already have cancer at hysterectomy

nodes.title: Biopsy report #4: adenocarcinoma
lines: Ontario: test every one for mismatch repair deficiency → genetic counselling ± testing

nodes.title: Spread
lines: direct: myometrium (common), cervix (fairly common)
lymphovascular → nodes, distant organs (rare) · transtubal → peritoneum (rare)

nodes.title: 3 · Minimally invasive
lines: uterine artery embolization · endometrial ablation

nodes.title: 4 · Surgery
lines: vaginal hysterectomy · laparoscopically assisted vaginal hysterectomy · total abdominal hysterectomy

nodes.title: Cause-specific: treat the endocrinopathy, deliver the baby
1 · Non-hormonal
lines: iron · cyclokapron (tranexamic acid, TXA) · ibuprofen

nodes.title: 2 · Hormonal
lines: OCP · Depo · Mirena · Visanne · GnRH agonist

nodes.title: Why hormones work
lines: progesterone (any type) = a 'lawnmower' for the endometrium: flow ↓ over time
Diane 35 + Yaz: anti-androgenic (PCOS) · Lupron (GnRH agonist): hypothalamic suppression

nodes.title: May need treatment
lines: mild: iron + reassurance
moderate: low-dose OCP, the best first line
severe/acute: serial hemoglobin, coagulation tests, IV estrogen

nodes.title: Stable
lines: estrogen + progesterone, or progesterone only · cyclokapron · imaging · referral
same options as reproductive age; avoid invasive surgery

nodes.title: Perimenopause: UNSTABLE
lines: IV fluids + airway, breathing, circulation + packed red blood cells
Foley catheter into the uterus to TAMPONADE
IV Premarin or high-dose oral estrogen if no contraindications; oral after 24 h
operating room if she cannot be stabilized

nodes.title: Usually the family physician
lines: nothing if symptoms are not troublesome
LOCAL ESTROGEN: vaginal cream, pill or ring
HRT: see the MENOPAUSE chart

nodes.title: Without atypia: MEDICAL
lines: progesterone: Megace, levonorgestrel intrauterine device
repeat biopsy, usually at 3 months
remove the cause: exogenous estrogen, weight loss

nodes.title: Atypical: SURGICAL
lines: hysterectomy + tubes and ovaries out (BSO)
high-dose progesterone only if surgery is ruled out; close follow-up

nodes.title: Staging by the pathologist after resection
lines: tumour, node, metastasis (TNM) → International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage: decides adjuvant treatment

nodes.title: Hysterectomy + BSO
lines: abdominal, laparoscopic or vaginal
higher grade or stage: lymphadenectomy, further staging, ± radiation, chemotherapy

panels.title: Reproductive age: choosing the agent
items: patient preference · cost · side effects · ease + efficacy over time
OCP: oral route often preferred, but needs daily remembering
Depo + Mirena: covered by ODSB, sustained therapy window, but an 'injection' or a 'foreign body'
Lupron: immediate and effective, but a high side-effect profile and very costly
TXA: non-hormonal, as needed only, but costly; reduces INTENSITY only, not duration or regularity

panels.title: Report #1: insufficient tissue
items: benign endocervical fragments, insufficient endometrial tissue
how much tissue depends on the procedure (blind, D&C, hysteroscopy) and the endometrium

panels.title: Refer to gynecology
items: PMB + risk factors for endometrial cancer
symptomatic or recurrent bleeding with focal pathology on biopsy (polyp)
PMB with endometrium > 5 mm or a 'vascular pedicle'

panels.title: Thickening found WITHOUT bleeding
items: no routine sampling: case by case on cancer risk factors
on tamoxifen: NO routine ultrasound for thickening
asymptomatic polyps: triage by size, age, risk factors
